title: lightweight-session-snapshot-layout-notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a compact, streaming-friendly session snapshot format that the client-side (edge) and server runtime can exchange. Idea: a small, versioned binary/JSON hybrid that supports incremental restore, partial fetch, and efficient KV cache reuse. This is intentionally lightweight — aimed at session resumption for interactive flows (chat/assistant) where restoring the full model state is expensive.

Goals (high level):
- Minimize bytes transferred for resumption while restoring determinism of past context (replies should not regress).
- Support partial restores (prefix-only, last N turns, or token-range).
- Allow incremental uploads (deltas) from client to server and server-to-client snapshots for mobile clients.
- Pluggable compression and optional encryption (KMS/HSM).
- Backwards-compatible versioning so older clients can still use limited semantics.

Format overview (conceptual):
- Top-level: JSON header (small, human readable) + binary payload sections.
- Header fields: version, session_id, model_id, last_seq, created_at, flags, section_index (list of offsets/lengths).
- Sections:
  1) session-metadata (JSON) -- user prefs, routing hints, pinned model variant, rollout token.
  2) prompt-pack (JSON or LZ4 compressed JSON) -- canonical prompt template + injected vars.
  3) kv-cache-chunks (binary) -- series of compressed KV cache segments with small headers (chunk id, start_pos, end_pos, checksum).
  4) token-index (binary) -- lightweight index mapping logical tokens to global token positions (optional).
  5) embeddings-snapshot (optional) -- only if we materialized client-side embeddings for reranking/citation. Stored separately and chunked.
  6) ops-log (delta list as JSON) -- append-only deltas for recent edits (useful for collaborative sessions).

Design notes / choices:
- Why header + sections? Allows streaming restore: client requests header (small JSON), decides to fetch only metadata + last N kv-cache chunks.
- Binary for KV cache: reduces size and parsing time; runtime can mmap or stream into GPU memory-friendly buffers.
- Chunking strategy: fixed-size token windows for predictable fetch (e.g., ~64KB payload chunks), but allow variable sized for compressed chunks.
- Checksums per chunk to enable partial re-download and resume.
- Versioning: header.version is semver-like (major.minor). Major bump = incompatible layout. Minor bump = add optional sections.

API shape sketches (server endpoints):
- GET /v1/sessions/{session_id}/snapshot?sections=header,meta,last-2-kv HTTP/1.1
  - returns multipart/stream with header JSON then requested sections.
  - streaming-friendly; first bytes are header so client can decide to cancel.

- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/snapshot (multipart/form-data or application/octet-stream)
  - body: header JSON + sections binary.
  - query flags: "delta=true" => server should apply deltas and merge.
  - response: 200 and new snapshot id / applied-delta-range.

Minimal header example (JSON):
{
  "version": "1.2",
  "session_id": "s-0a1b2c3d",
  "model_id": "rwd-m-13b-q4",
  "last_seq": "turn-13",
  "created_at": "2024-11-19T15:04:12Z",
  "flags": ["encrypted"],
  "sections": [
    {"name": "session-metadata", "off": 256, "len": 1024, "hash": "sha256:abcd..."},
    {"name": "kv-cache-0", "off": 1280, "len": 65536, "hash": "sha256:ef01..."}
  ]
}

Binary chunk header (per-chunk):
- u16: chunk flags (compression, last-chunk)
- u32: token_start_pos
- u32: token_end_pos
- u32: compressed_length
- u32: uncompressed_length
- u8[32]: checksum (sha256)
- followed by compressed payload bytes

Restoration semantics / partial fetch policies:
- Typical restore path for mobile: fetch header -> fetch session-metadata + prompt-pack -> fetch last N kv-cache chunks covering last ~2048 tokens -> resume decoding locally.
- Server-side rapid resume: server stores uncompressed in a memory-mapped pool, but exposes compressed chunks to clients.
- If client lacks model variant, server can fall back to text-only prompt-pack restore (stateless).

Compatibility and migration:
- Keep header small so older clients can at least get metadata and choose to continue without full restore.
- Consider an explicit "compatibility-mode" flag where server provides a flattened JSON conversation as fallback.

Security / encryption:
- Option A: envelope encryption per snapshot with KMS-wrapped DEK. Header lists KMS key id and encrypted DEK blob.
- Option B: TLS-only for in-transit + default server-side encryption at rest.
- For mobile offline stored snapshots, require local encrypted store integration and optionally HSM-bound keys (enterprise).

Performance considerations:
- Use streaming compression (LZ4) with chunk sizes tuned for typical mobile bandwidth (8–64KB compressed).
- Make chunk boundaries align with KV cache block boundaries to avoid cache invalidation during partial restore.
- Avoid storing large embedding arrays inline if they can be referenced from a separate content store by id.

Edge cases / failure modes:
- Corrupted chunk -> fallback to earlier snapshot or request server fallback to flattened JSON conversation.
- Incompatible model_id -> server may attempt automatic mapping to a compatible variant; if impossible, reject restore with clear error that includes required model fingerprint.
- Concurrent delta uploads: serialize with per-session op-log version; server applies last-write-wins unless client requests optimistic-merge.

Example cURL (download header only):
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sessions/s-0a1b2c3d/snapshot?sections=header"

ASCII diagram (streaming flow):
[client] -- GET header --> [server]
  read header -> decide needed sections
[client] -- GET requested sections (range queries / multipart) --> [server]
  server streams sections as they become available
[client] -- apply chunks to local state -> resume decoding -> continue session

Open questions / TODO (short):
- T1: How to represent token positions consistently across quantized-model variants? Need global token index or model-agnostic offset.
- T2: Decide canonical compression: LZ4 vs Zstd (latency vs density). Run microbenchmarks with realistic kv-cache blobs.
- T3: Snapshot TTL and retention policy for GDPR/CCPA. Must provide deletion API for snapshots.
- T4: Offload big arrays (embeddings) to separate content-addressed store and include CID refs in header.
- T5: Define server-side migration: when major layout changes, how to convert existing stored snapshots without full re-encode?

Notes to self:
- Share with SRE for bandwidth/egress cost estimates.
- Sync with mobile SDK owners (Lina) to ensure simple restore API.
- Prototype: create a toy snapshot writer/reader in runtime repo; include both JSON header and fake binary chunks.

Rough timeline (for personal roadmap):
- Week 0: small PoC writer + reader, produce 3 sample snapshots from runtime.
- Week 1: benchmarks on chunk sizes and compression.
- Week 2: basic server endpoints + streaming response.
- Week 3: mobile SDK integration test.

End of scratchpad.

(Looser notes and fragments below)
- half-formed idea: delta compression using token-diff + reference to previous snapshot id -> send only changed KV blocks.
- thought: for private deployments, allow "local-only" snapshots that never leave device; runtime should accept local restore via signed CSR to prove authenticity.
- question: do we expose snapshot metadata in Console? Might be useful for debugging but leaks context; default to hashed ids only.
